title: Microbatch fragmentation and KV-cache cold misses causing transient mid-p99 latency spikes
creator: Maya Chen
description: Summary: Production observed recurring mid-p99 latency spikes (~200-400ms extra) intermittently across several Dedicated GPU pools serving mixed-quant workloads. Spikes started 2026-02-17 after a scheduler heuristic change that introduced stochastic probe sampling. Initial mitigation (rate-limiting probes) reduced frequency but did not fully eliminate spikes. This ticket tracks investigation, short-term mitigations, and long-term hardening to prevent microbatch fragmentation and KV-cache cold misses tied to kernel selection jitter.
timeline: 2026-02-17 09:23 UTC: Oncall alert - p99 latency for dedicated-pool-eu-west crossed 1.2s threshold. Automatic rollback not triggered because throughput SLOs were met.
2026-02-17 09:45 UTC: Eng oncall confirmed spike correlated with a surge of small requests and increased probe activity from path-selector v2 heuristic (deployed 2026-02-16).
2026-02-17 10:30 UTC: Emergency mitigation - throttled probe sampler and increased probe backoff window. Immediate p99 improvement observed but residual spikes persisted.

2026-02-18 15:00 UTC: Reproduced at scale in staging with synthetic mixed-quant workload; observed microbatch fragmentation where microbatches split across kernel candidates and caused KV-cache churn.

2026-02-19 12:00 UTC: Root cause hypothesis refined to interaction between stochastic probe sampling, dynamic kernel re-ranking, and KV-cache warmup expectation leading to cold misses and microbatch serialization delays.
2026-03-05 16:00 UTC: Canary rollout of deterministic probe gating and probe token-budget cap (canary in us-west) showed >95% reduction in triggered fragmentation events.
2026-03-10 11:00 UTC: Decision to proceed with scheduled runtime patch and expand observability. This ticket coordinates the rollout and follow-ups.
root_cause: Scheduler path-selector v2 introduced randomized probe sampling to explore kernel candidates under changing load patterns.

Probe sampling sometimes selected multiple incompatible kernel candidates for adjacent microbatches, which caused microbatch fragmentation (single logical request split across differently ranked kernels).

Fragmentation caused duplicate KV-cache entries and eviction churn; warm KV-cache expectations were violated and subsequent token generation incurred cache misses and re-warm costs, increasing p95/p99 latency.
Mixed-quant workloads amplified the effect because candidate kernels had substantially different memory layouts and quantization code paths, increasing the cost of switching execution paths.
Telemetry lacked a concise signal that correlated probe-sampling events to KV-cache miss rate and microbatch boundary splintering, delaying root-cause discovery.
short_term_mitigation: Throttle probe sampler (deployed 2026-02-17) to reduce probe rate under high concurrency.
Introduce probe token-budget cap per worker and an immediate probe backoff when microbatch splitting is detected (canary-deployed 2026-03-05).
Add emergency SLA-driven circuit-breaker: if KV-cache miss-rate delta > 10% over baseline, force deterministic kernel selection and disable exploratory probes for 5 minutes.
Patch path-selector to prefer kernel affinity across contiguous microbatches within the same request to avoid splitting.
long_term_actions: Deterministic kernel-ranking mode behind feature flag and canary rollout; default to deterministic for Dedicated customers with strict latency SLOs.
Rework probe sampling so that probes are grouped by request and limited to a single candidate per request when latency budgets are tight.
KV-cache telemetry enrichment: add per-request cache-warmth metric, microbatch-boundary kernel-change signal, and a synthetic 'probe-induced-coldmiss' alert rule.

Develop a regression harness that runs mixed-quant traces and measures fragmentation, KV miss-rate, and p95/p99 under controlled probe configurations. Automate as part of PR gating for scheduler heuristics.
Bench: quantify penalty of kernel switches for common mixed-quant model families and publish kernel switch cost matrix to runtime heuristics for informed scoring.
Design and ship an admission control policy that pre-classifies requests likely to cause fragmentation and routes them to low-variance execution lanes (e.g., fixed-kernel workers).

replication_steps: 1) In staging, deploy path-selector v2 and configure probe sampler rate to match production settings (see config/probes.yaml).
2) Generate mixed-quant workload using synthetic-client with distribution: 60% short prompts (<=64 tokens), 40% long prompts (>=512 tokens), Q8 and Q4 model variants mixed at 1:3 ratio.
3) Ramp concurrency to 250qps focused on dedicated microworker pool. Observe microbatch grouping and kernel assignment traces in /traces/runtime/probe_events.

4) Compare KV-cache per-worker warmness and eviction rate with and without stochastic probes enabled. Expect to see increased evictions and higher per-token latency when probes are enabled and fragmentation occurs.
5) Re-run with deterministic probe gating to confirm reduction in microbatch fragmentation and p99 latency.

sql:select bucket, p50, p95, p99 from token_latency where probe_flag=true group by bucket - compare latency distribution when probes fired
